Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
GYMNASTIC EQUIPMENT — LANDING MATS 

( 2 000 mm x 1 250 mm x 60 mm ) 

[ ISO Title : Gymnastic Equipment — Landing Mats 

( 2 GOD mm x 1 250 mm x 60 mm ) ] 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



National Foreword 

This Indian Standard, which is identical with ISO 5905-1980 ' Gymnastic equipment — Landing 
mats ( 2 000 mm x 1 250 mm x 60 mm )' issued by the International Organization for Standardization 
(ISO), was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on the recommendation of the Sports Goods 
Sectional Committee and approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division 
Council. 

Comma (,) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards the current practice is 
to use a point ( . ) as the decimal marker.

read as 'Indian Standard'.

Indian Standards are also given. Read the corresponding Indian Standard wherever a reference to an 
International Standard appears:

1 Scops and field of application 

This International Standard specifies the charac- 
teristics of landing mats of dimensions 2 000 mm 
XI 250 mmx60 mm for use in competitions and 
training. The determination of th£S3 characteris- 
tics shall ensure that 

a) for competitions and training, mats ate used, 
the hardness, shock absorption and resistance 
to slipping of the landing surface of which 
lie in a specified range, depending on their use; 

b) the risk of injury to the gymnast, by slipping, 
is reduced. 

2 References 

\S0 5903, Gymnast/c equipment — Landing mats 
and surfaces for floor exercises — Determination 
of hardness and impact damping. 

\S0 5904r Gymnastic equipment — Landing mats 
and surfaces for floor exercises — Determination 
of resistance to slipping. 

3 Dimensions 

The dimensions of the landing mat shall be those 
indicated in the figure 1 . 

Dimensions in millimetres 




Figure 1 — Dimensions of landing mat 



4 Material 

The manufacturer is free to choose the material for 
the mat made in one piece, or with core and cover, 
observing, however, the requirements on hardness 
and shock absorption and resistance to slipping 
given in this International Standard, 

5 Manufacture 



5.1 Landing surfaces 

The surface layer of the landing surface shall be 
such that there is only a slight extension when the 
gymnast rebounds. It shall be marked on the mat 
which surface is the landing surface if only one 
surface of the mat i^s to be regarded as the landing 
surface corresponding to the requirements in 7.2. 



5.2 Lateral faces 

The lateral faces of the mats shall be perpendicular 
to the landing surface. 



6.3 Loops and handles 

If the landing mat is provided with loops or hand- 
les for handling, they shall be fixed in such a way 
that the mats can be placed side-by-side without 
any gaps. 

6 Design 

According to the choice of the manufacturer, the 
landing mat may consist of core and cover or of 
one piece. If a cover is provided, it shall be firmly 
attached to the core or be designed so that no 
slipping between core and cover occurs when the 
mat is in use. 



Reinforcing and other bands shall be fixed so as to 
comply with the requirements on hardness and 
shock absorption (see 7.1). 



IS : 10831 -1984 
ISO 5905-1980 



7 Requirements and tests 

7.1 Hardness and shock absorption 

The determination of hardness and shock absorp- 
tion shall be carried out in accordance with ISO 
5903.

The measurements shall be carried out on one mat 
at nine measuring points symmetrically distributed 
on the landing surface; if necessary, at least two 
measuring points shall be placed in the area of 
the reinforcing or other bands. 



If indications concerning the number N of 
rebounds after the first impact on the mat and 
concerning the coefficient of shock absorption € 
are required, see ISO 5903. 



7.2 Resistance to slipping of the landing 
surface 



The determination of resistance to slipping shall be 
carried out in accordance with ISO 5904.
